attribution: Head of Buddha, The Fralin Museum of Art; 3D data by Matthew Schneider and Will Rourk, University of Virginia Library. CC0 1.0.
sourceArtifact: Head of Buddha, 2nd–3rd century, Swat Valley, Pakistan, unknown Gandharan artist. This is a different historical artifact used as an anatomical modeling base, not claimed as the photographed altar statue.

transformations.description: The verified source and import matrix already use +Y up and +Z front. Fit those actual axes directly with nonuniform dimensions; taper neck below Y2.53; extend lateral rear auricles; trim above Y3.32 and below Y2.40; retain the real jaw above Y2.46 and blend only the lower 6cm neck bearing into the existing ringed throat; cap cuts; restore the eroded urna socket with finite cast geometry; mildly smooth; union into body/hand/robe with 4.5mm model voxels and decimate. The rejected r8-01 inversion came from misreading an isolated inspection camera with an automatic pi roll, not an import transform.
transformations.topologyRepair: Weld duplicate procedural meridians before bisecting, close all cut loops, and recalculate consistent outward component winding before the real voxel union.
referenceLedSculptureRepairs: Preserve the actual scanned jaw and chin; extend its real neck down to Y2.40 and blend only Y2.40–2.46 into the grooved throat. This avoids both the flat clipped shelf and an overlong artificial jaw taper.
Retain actual concha/helix anatomy, shorten pointed lower scan tips, and union rounded auricle lobes.
Sculpt the eroded forehead socket toward a continuous forehead plane, then add the small finite cast urna bead.
